 Flooding in Christmas leaves roads, yards underwater as family worries about more rain
 A woman says her family has only seen flooding this severe about three times in 52 years
 Alex Cook , Community Correspondent
 Published:  November 20, 2026 at 5:20 PM Tags:  Christmas , Orange County , Flooding , Weather ORANGE COUNTY, Fla. – Floodwaters continue to cover portions of Fort Christmas Road and nearby properties in East Orange County, creating problems for homeowners as more rain remains possible this weekend.
 On Friday, News 6 found stretches of roadway covered in standing water, with vehicles driving through flooded sections and water extending into residential front yards.
 Joy Hushing was visiting her 84-year-old mother, who has lived along Fort Christmas Road for 52 years.
 Hushing said her mother uses a walker, making it difficult to navigate her flooded property. Even something as simple as getting the mail has become a challenge.
 “I’ve had to go to the post office. I had to get her mail down there because they couldn’t deliver it to a mailbox,” Hushing said.
 The flooding is also interfering with her mother’s ability to care for a family pony that belonged to her late husband.
 “She’s got a pony back there to feed, so somebody else has to come and feed him if she can’t get out there,” Hushing said.
 Hushing said the pony is about 25 years old and that her mother normally brings him apples twice a day.
 Although the family’s elevated home has remained dry, much of the surrounding property has been underwater.
 Hushing said the water was even higher Thursday and that flooding this severe has been rare during her family’s five decades in the area.
 “This is the third time this has happened with her,” Hushing said.
 She believes drainage problems may be contributing to the flooding and wants Orange County to inspect nearby ditches.
 She’s also concerned about drivers traveling too quickly through the standing water, sending waves toward her mother’s property.
 “If county could come out, at least put signs telling people slow down right in front of here, because that’s what worries me,” Hushing said.
 A nearby homeowner told News 6 that her elevated house had avoided flooding, but the surrounding pastures were deeply flooded.
 The National Weather Service said Friday afternoon that rainfall was diminishing across east Central Florida. However, scattered showers remain possible Saturday, with additional rainfall potentially aggravating areas already affected by flooding.
 For Hushing, the hope is that the water continues to drop before the next round of rain arrives.
